analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Fed. Hyperscalers. UK Budget. Cross asset Sentiment 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: SK Hynix reported a big beat overnight and the stock rose about 10%. Revenue +32% sequentially, operating profit +38%, margins at 80%, and more than half of 2027/28 capacity is already under long term agreements. The semi tape is bid.

A series of positive developments this week is easing financing concerns. Per Privorotsky, the demand side never really changed. The debate was about supply, financing and a Street-wide risk reduction exercise, which left some of the lowest net exposures all year and among the largest two week institutional tech liquidations on record.

Early signs of buying appeared yesterday, with people picking up parts of the semi complex and some demand for upside vol. Privorotsky says it is early and people have barely begun to re-risk. So far this is the abatement of supply rather than meaningful fresh demand.

Fed: no projections at this meeting, so focus is on the vote, the statement and Warsh. A hold is fully priced. Two dissents are probably the central expectation. Zero dissents would be a dovish surprise and three would reinforce December as the next hike.

Privorotsky's guess is that the Fed sets up December without committing. The harder question is how far the hiking cycle extends after that. Watch for acknowledgment of tighter financial conditions or softer employment in the statement, and watch the long end if the message sounds too soft on forward inflation. Not much event risk is priced in equities.

Microsoft and Google earnings matter most today. Buyside expectations are probably near high-40s% Azure growth and mid-90s% Google Cloud growth. The question is whether results beat already high expectations. Azure probably needs a guidance raise to be properly supportive.

A miss on capacity, meaning the companies cannot bring enough compute online, would hurt near term revenue but could be more bullish for the scarcity premium and future spending. Watch customer concentration, demand breadth, and the relationship between revenue growth, capex and margins.

UK Budget is today with limited fiscal headroom and a need for new revenue. Possible measures include bank taxes, gambling levies, property related measures and support for first time buyers. Banks are particularly sensitive. The OBR forecasts and gilt reaction matter as much as the headline measures.

Middle East: oil is bouncing again. Gulf equities rallied sharply yesterday on regional collective bargaining, then opened lower after the WSJ reported Washington warned Gulf allies to prepare for a potentially short, aggressive campaign against Iran after the midterms. No final decision has been made.
Israel's election looks deadlocked. Likud outperformed some expectations but neither bloc has a clear majority, so weeks of coalition uncertainty may follow.

Risk view: Privorotsky argues the market got extraordinarily pessimistic on AI, took nets too low, and is now getting a series of positive developments. Confidence is low, positioning is light and AI micro is improving. Credit traded much better yesterday and remains his focal point.

Privorotsky thinks gross exposure can start working again in the right pockets of tech. He still wants selectivity given the macro, and says the set up into year end is cleaner once the macro headwinds pass. Energy is elevated, geopolitics are unresolved and the midterms are next week.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers monetize traffic, compute and infrastructure volumes that remain robust, which should speed cloud growth, backlog conversion and cash generation. A capacity-driven miss would raise the scarcity premium and future spending.
tension_points.bear_case: Expectations are already very high, and a miss on compute capacity would disappoint near term revenue. The market also wants evidence that incremental economics work given capex and margins.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Azure without a guidance raise, or revenue growth that fails to justify capex and margins.

tension_points.bull_case: Financial conditions have tightened, payroll growth is weak and housing is cooling, leaving room for a more balanced message.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation is stubborn and three dissents would reinforce December as the next hike, with the long end at risk if the message is too soft on forward inflation.
